model_output.exposed_thinking: We need schedule minimizing sum of completion times (total flow time). Single machine, no preemption. We have precedence constraints: A before C, B before E. We need to find order that respects constraints and minimizes sum of completion times. This is classic scheduling with precedence constraints minimizing sum of completion times: optimal is to use Smith's rule? Actually for minimizing sum of completion times with precedence constraints, the optimal schedule is to use a priority rule: at each step, among available jobs, pick the one with smallest processing time (SPT). Because all weights equal. So we can simulate: Initially available jobs: A, B (since C requires A, E requires B). Also D has no constraints. So available: A(1), B(4), D(5). Choose smallest: A. Schedule A first. After A completes, C becomes available. Now available: B(4), C(2), D(5). Choose smallest: C(2). After C, no new. Available: B(4), D(5). Choose B(4). After B, E becomes available. Available: D(5), E(3). Choose E(3). Then D(5). So order: A, C, B, E, D. Check if any tie? No. So output "A,C,B,E,D".
